answer: Give every account a unique spiral route printed in ferrous ink across one page of a shared atlas, with waypoints only that account may claim. At a random hour, the account must photograph its atlas page beside a live compass, showing the needle deflecting at each ferrous waypoint, plus a handwritten note naming the next waypoint. Two other route-holders verify the deflection matches the atlas and the handwriting matches earlier notes. A Sybil farm would need a distinct printed atlas, a compass, and a distinct hand per account, so each fake identity costs real materials and time.
